lines.en: Hana, this fair is so lively! **What do people usually do** for festivals in Korea?
lines.pt: Hana, esta feira está tão animada! O que as pessoas costumam fazer nos festivais na Coreia?

lines.en: **In my country,** we celebrate Seollal, the Lunar New Year. **People usually** wear hanbok and visit their families.
lines.pt: No meu país, comemoramos o Seollal, o Ano Novo Lunar. As pessoas costumam usar hanbok e visitar a família.

lines.en: Nice! What do you eat then?
lines.pt: Legal! O que vocês comem nessa data?

lines.en: **We eat** tteokguk, a rice cake soup. We also bow to our elders to show respect.
lines.pt: Comemos tteokguk, uma sopa de bolinho de arroz. Também fazemos reverência aos mais velhos para mostrar respeito.

lines.en: Interesting! **In Spain,** on New Year’s Eve, we eat twelve grapes at midnight.
lines.pt: Interessante! Na Espanha, na véspera de Ano Novo, comemos doze uvas à meia-noite.

lines.en: One grape for each chime of the clock. **It’s supposed to** bring good luck for the new year.
lines.pt: Uma uva para cada badalada do relógio. Dizem que traz sorte para o ano novo.

lines.en: I love that! We don’t do that in Korea, but I’d like to try it.
lines.pt: Adorei! Não fazemos isso na Coreia, mas eu gostaria de experimentar.

lines.en: Come to my place next December. **We’ll celebrate** together!
lines.pt: Venha à minha casa em dezembro. Vamos comemorar juntos!

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Sharing traditions
pages.intro: Talking about traditions is a warm way to connect with people from other cultures. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: Families gather for the Lunar New Year, bow to elders and eat tteokguk.
On New Year’s Eve many people eat twelve grapes at midnight, one for each chime.
Special dishes often carry meaning: luck, family or respect.

qs.q: Why do people say “usually” when describing traditions?
qs.pt: Por que se diz “usually” ao descrever tradições?

levels.A2: Because not everyone does the same thing.
levels.B1: It avoids generalizing: traditions vary between families and regions.
levels.B2: It acknowledges variation within a culture and keeps the description accurate and respectful.

qs.q: How can you show interest in someone’s tradition?
qs.pt: Como demonstrar interesse na tradição de alguém?

levels.B1: Ask about the meaning and say you would like to try it.
levels.B2: Ask open questions about meaning and personal experience, and avoid judging.
“Strange” can sound judgmental; “different”, “unfamiliar” or “interesting” keep a respectful tone.

pages.compare: In Brazil, people share traditions such as New Year’s Eve clothes in white and festas juninas. In English you say “In my country…” and “People usually…”. What tradition would you present?

teach.goal: Mostrar como descrever tradições com respeito e curiosidade.

extra: What is a tradition from your region?

stretch: B2: discuta como não generalizar sobre uma cultura.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In English one syllable is stronger: CELebrate, TRAdition, FESTival. The wrong stress can make a word hard to understand.

own.prompt: Write one sentence about a tradition with a three-syllable word.
own.criteria: Say it twice: mark the stressed syllable with your hand. Did the word sound natural?

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The situation stays the same; the language grows in length, nuance and autonomy.

ladder.goal: Name a festival with key words.

ladder.say: In my country, we celebrate Carnival. People usually dance.
In my country, people usually celebrate with family, and it’s supposed to bring good luck.
Although traditions vary by region, most families celebrate by gathering, and the food usually has a symbolic meaning.
What strikes visitors is how a ritual that seems purely festive is, for many families, a quiet way of honoring those who came before.
It is a custom that wears its meaning lightly: you take part first, and only later does it dawn on you what you have inherited.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.
